name: Nous Research
subcategory: open-weight model fine-tunes (Hermes), decentralised training (Psyche), open-source agent (Hermes Agent)
origin_detail: Began in 2022 as a volunteer open-source research collective whose members met on Discord, GitHub and Twitter, releasing the Hermes series of fine-tunes of Meta's Llama and Mistral models; incorporated in 2023 by Jeffrey Quesnelle, Karan Malhotra, Ryan Teknium and Shivani Mitra (VentureBeat also names Bowen Peng). Described by Wikipedia as an American AI company.
flagship_projects: Psyche decentralised training network (Apache-2.0, on Solana)
openness_notes: Initial 1: the early Hermes releases were fine-tunes whose weights inherit Meta's licences. Nous-Hermes-13b (2023-06-03) is labelled 'gpl' on Hugging Face but is a LLaMA fine-tune, and Nous-Hermes-Llama2-13b (2023-07-20) is labelled 'mit' but tagged llama-2, so the Meta licence governs (level 1 on the AI scale). Current 2: the largest Hermes 4 models (405B, 2025-08-06) are still under the 'llama3' licence (level 1), but Hermes 4 14B is Apache-2.0 (Qwen3 base), Psyche is Apache-2.0, and the flagship since February 2026, Hermes Agent, is MIT. Money comes from a hosted Hermes Agent ($20-$200/month), the Nous Portal model API and a planned commercial 'Hermes for Businesses', so open core.

license_history.note: Nous-Hermes-13b, created 2023-06-03; the base model's licence governs regardless of the card label

license_history.license: Llama 2 Community Licence-derived weights (HF card says 'mit')

license_history.note: Hermes-4-405B created 2025-08-06 on Llama-3.1-405B; Hermes-4-14B created 2025-08-30 on Qwen3-14B
Repo created 2025-07-22, public release February 2026; ~266K GitHub stars and ~60K forks by 2026-11-24; hosted version sold on paid tiers

risk_events: Crypto incentives: Psyche training network on Solana with token rewards; the April 2025 $1B valuation was for a planned token, not equity; Fortune noted wariness of crypto in AI research and Malhotra acknowledged 'a lot of room for grift'
May 2026: a Cloud Security Alliance note described an audit finding four critical and nine high-severity issues in Hermes Agent's default configuration (per Wikipedia)
Largest models depend on Meta's Llama licence, which Nous cannot relicense
Valuation of $1.5B (Oct 2026) reported by the WSJ, not disclosed by the company
robustness: Hermes Agent (MIT, ~266K stars, ~60K forks) and Psyche (Apache-2.0) could survive the company; the Llama-derived weights carry Meta's terms. Governance is a single VC-backed company; Psyche is published under a separate PsycheFoundation GitHub organisation.
physical_science_relevance: Indirect: general-purpose open agent and models; DisTrO, which cut per-step data exchanged between GPUs about 857-fold in one preliminary test, could lower the cost of training domain models across institutions.
openness_effect_assessment: Openness turned a volunteer Discord community into a VC-backed lab: about $20M of seed money (2024), a $50M Paradigm round at a $1B token valuation (Apr 2025) and a $90M round at a reported $1.5B (Oct 2026). The step change came from the MIT-licensed Hermes Agent, which Nous says was cloned more than 24 million times since February 2026, monetised through paid hosting, not from its Llama-licensed models.
key_takeaway: Nous Research is the community-origin case in this group: open fine-tunes and crypto-funded decentralised training attracted capital, but the licence that mattered commercially was MIT on an agent framework, sold as a hosted service ($20-$200/month) with an enterprise edition planned. Its biggest model weights, as Llama derivatives, stayed at level 1.
